strategy.mode: metadata-first, deterministic, OpenAIRE-aligned export plus richer internal JSON
strategy.title_policy: Single export title only. Multilingual or alternative titles are preserved in internal.title_variants.
strategy.language_policy: dc:language is treated as the resource language. Multilingual metadata literal languages are tracked separately in internal.metadata_languages.
strategy.dates_policy: Export dates are limited to Accepted, Available, Issued. Available falls back to Issued when absent. Submitted, Created and Modified stay in internal.internal_dates.
strategy.alternate_identifier_policy: Internal article IDs are not exported as OpenAIRE alternateIdentifiers; they are preserved only in internal.article_ID/object_ID.
strategy.description_policy: Preserve multilingual DC.Description entries when present.
strategy.files_policy: citation_pdf_url is preferred for oaire:file/fulltext extraction; viewer URLs are deterministically converted to download URLs for internal PDF assets and local PDF saving.
strategy.references_policy: All citation_reference values are preserved as supplemental data; no promotion to OpenAIRE relatedIdentifier.
strategy.warning_diagnostics_policy: If enabled, warnings can trigger an advisory OpenAI call with automatic second attempt and user-controlled further retry loop; AI output is supplemental and never mutates extracted metadata automatically.

title.datacite:title: Towards inclusive universities: Promoting self-advocacy and active citizenship for students with disabilities and Specific Learning Disorders

descriptions.value: The pursuit of inclusion in higher education requires reevaluating the roles and practices of universities. While institutions are increasingly recognized as essential agents in promoting social equity and community well-being, students with disabilities and Specific Learning Disorders continue to encounter barriers that prevent their full participation in academic and civic life. These challenges highlight the shortcomings of current approaches and emphasize the need for systemic innovations that prioritize both citizenship and active engagement. In this context, the University of Macerata has launched a project aimed at including students with disabilities and Specific Learning Disorders, seeking to develop transformative strategies that align educational equity with broader objectives of promoting community development and welfare.

The pursuit of inclusion in higher education requires reevaluating the roles and practices of universities. While institutions are increasingly recognized as essential agents in promoting social equity and community well-being, students with disabilities and Specific Learning Disorders continue to encounter barriers that prevent their full participation in academic and civic life. These challenges highlight the shortcomings of current approaches and emphasize the need for systemic innovations that prioritize both citizenship and active engagement. In this context, the University of Macerata has launched a project aimed at including students with disabilities and Specific Learning Disorders, seeking to develop transformative strategies that align educational equity with broader objectives of promoting community development and welfare.
